properties.name: All fourteen unreachable holes are closed: eight constructors gain parameters and Actor gets the constructor it never had
properties.rationale:
Anthony asked for all fourteen, which also answers the question that had been left open for Actor: it should be user-writable, because two of the fourteen are its properties and there is no other way to reach them.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO. It does not make anybody state these things. It removes the reason they could not, which is the only half a tool can honestly supply — the same bound the contract-enforcement brainstorm records for standards and typings. And the remaining 28 unreachable properties stay unreachable ON PURPOSE: 15 are written by an operation, where a caller parameter would let somebody forge a computed fact, and 13 are carried by nothing at all.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary:
The reachability report now reads 0 HOLE. It was 14 before this, and 43 before the split by intent separated a hole from a property an operation writes.

WHAT GAINED A PARAMETER. add_capability takes tier, is_entry_point and is_exit_point — the two flags are the capability's own, distinct from Flow.entry_point which names a capability from the flow's side, and 147 of 234 capabilities carried them through the generic escape hatch. add_component and add_flow take tier. add_constraint takes concern and priority, both carried by all seven constraints. add_requirement takes concern, carried by 154 of 207. add_interface takes spec, the free-text detail its structured fields do not carry, carried by 13 of 22. add_project takes decomposition_levels — THE SHARPEST OF THE FOURTEEN, because hierarchy.rs reads the design's own ladder on every level check and nothing could write it. link_artifact takes content_ref and note_kind, which are FRAGMENT fields and are therefore set where the fragment is minted rather than through a separate tool.

AND ONE IS A NEW TOOL RATHER THAN A PARAMETER. add_actor did not exist, so Actor's two properties were unreachable for one reason: there was nothing to give a parameter to. Actor is one of three types in that state; the other two, EnvironmentRule and QualityGate, have no instances anywhere and so never reached the unreachable list at all. Whether they should get constructors is still open.

ONE SHARED HELPER writes every optional property a core constructor does not take. That placement is the point rather than tidiness: this whole family survived because each hole was fixed where it was reported and the siblings were never asked, so one place to change is the correction. The list and the bool pair need their own writes because the helper takes strings.

OMITTING ANY OF THEM CHANGES NOTHING and a test pins it: an unstated flag stays unstated, because absence means nobody said. These add a way to SAY, never an obligation to.

FAILING FIRST, OBSERVED: ten tests written before the parameters existed, failing on the missing add_actor and then on nine assertions. All ten pass. Each asserts the value reaches the STORED PROPERTY rather than that the call was accepted, because a tool that takes a field and drops it passes a signature check and still fails the caller.

MECHANICAL COST, recorded because it is the risky part: 30 LinkArtifactOptions literals and 131 request-struct fields across the test suite needed the new fields. Two regex attempts corrupted struct definitions and misplaced fields past a literal's closing brace before a brace-matched patcher with a definition guard worked. Both CI job shapes were run locally before pushing this time.
